metadata.evidence: # Ditch the Gold Standard: Re-evaluating Conversational Question Answering
metadata.reason: Primary title of the repository and the corresponding research paper.

metadata.value: In this work, we conduct the first large-scale human evaluation of state-of-the-art conversational QA systems.

metadata.evidence: This is the repository for our ACL'2022 paper
metadata.reason: Indicates the conference and year where the work was published.

metadata.evidence: [Ditch the Gold Standard: Re-evaluating Conversational Question Answering](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.08812.pdf)
metadata.reason: Direct link to the arXiv version of the paper.

metadata.evidence: Our experiments use [QuAC dataset](https://quac.ai) for passages and conversations, and the test set of [CANARD dataset](https://sites.google.com/view/qanta/projects/canard) for context-independent questions in `Auto-Replace`.
metadata.reason: Lists external datasets required to reproduce the experiments.

metadata.evidence: You can download the human annotation dataset from `data/human_annotation_data.json`.
metadata.reason: Path to the newly released human-annotated dataset included in the repository.
Standard command to install Python dependencies listed in the project.

metadata.evidence: We provide a convenient interface to test model performance on a few evaluation protocols compared in our paper, including `Auto-Pred`, `Auto-Replace` and our proposed evaluation protocol, `Auto-Rewrite`
metadata.reason: Identifies the specific evaluation methodologies implemented in the codebase.

metadata.evidence: We provide our implementations for the four models that we used in our paper: BERT, [GraphFlow](https://www.ijcai.org/Proceedings/2020/171), [HAM](https://dl.acm.org/doi/abs/10.1145/3357384.3357905), [ExCorD](https://aclanthology.org/2021.acl-long.478/).
metadata.reason: Names the baseline models whose implementations are provided for evaluation.
